For example, I've seen a really crazy close up UFO encounter where my vehicle got chased. I don't assume it was aliens; I just accept that there is no good explanation. I've also observed people and objects behaving in a way that post hoc reasoning would suggest was due to my desire for them to do so. I don't assume I have psychic powers though, just that it's coincidence and confirmation bias.

My point is that everyone sees weird stuff that from their perspective is best explained supernaturally. It's a rare person who admits they're not as reliable of a witness as they might wish and constrains their explanations to well supported phenomenon. It hurts one's pride a bit.

What are your tips for a Civ V beginner?

Wear a butt plug. It'll help you focus.

Set cities to prioritize production, then manually have the city work the tile with the most food.

Growth and science are the two most important things for any victory condition. Everything else comes second.

Internal trade routes are the best.

Install the enhanced user interface mod.

Bribe the ai's to go to war with each other. Try paying the guy with the biggest army to attack one of the smaller civs. If you have to go to war, try and get someone to pay you for it.

Sell extra strategic resources one at a time for 2 gp a turn.

And if you don't exercise and play too much civ, I made this routine a couple of days ago I'd cut out the vacuum holds, they were kinda useless. The routine isn't as optimized as it could be, but it keeps me moving.

Internal trade routes are the best.

Venice, tho?

Nah, that's actually a legitimate strategy for Venice; use your extra trade routes for internal ones. Whenever you get a Merchant, buy a nearby city state. Buyout a granary and send a trade unit there, then immediately start sending food back to Venice. Try to get as many Merchants as you possibly can early game.

Venice itself will become absolutely fucking enormous. I regularly get to 50 population when other capitals are at 20, maximum. Once you have enough citizens to work every tile and every specialist slot, flip all your city-state internal routes to production. You can now build wonders so fast that no one can keep up. Also, you can produce almost every unit in 1 or 2 turns.

Venice can make more than enough gold per turn with the standard number of trade routes. And if you get the Statue of Liberty, it's totally over. 100% of the time.
Don't be afraid to restart if you get shitty start location.

You'll usually start next to either a ton of 1 luxury resource, or a smaller amount of 2. If both of them require a 2nd-tier tech (so you have to research something else first to unlock the tech you need) to harvest, you should probably restart. That's what we call a shitty starting location.
